reviews.title: bait-and-switch. Avoid.
reviews.text: Most workout apps hide their pre-made routines behind a paywall, which is standard. But virtually every app still lets you create and track your own custom exercises for free. This app takes greed to a whole new level. At first, it lets you log your own workouts while locking the pre-made ones. But once you actually commit to using it, it suddenly paywalls your own custom exercises too! Holding a user’s basic workout logging hostage after letting them set it up is pure bait-and-switch. Don't waste your time logging anything here—you'll just get locked out of your own data later.

reviews.title: I’m sure that it is a great app…
reviews.text: …once you learn how to use it.  To me, personally, it’s just not user friendly to me.  Maybe it’s me but I cannot figure out where to log everything.  I log it in one place the rest timer timer doesn’t start, I push a button (which one I don’t know?) and another place to log pops up and then, when I think I”m finished, I press the forward error, it doesn’t go to the next exercise and asks me if I want to save changes permanently.  I don’t know.  Then, at the end of the workout, instead of showing all six exercises that I started with, it showed two. It’s just not easy unless you memorize the “owners manual” before using.  I prefer not to have to stop my routine after every exercise to figure out how to log my sets/reps.  Might as well get out the notebook that I use to use in the early 90’s.  It’s faster…

reviews.title: Revamp this app and the CS reps
reviews.text:
The features on this app are subpar compared to what they advertise…AI must mean advanced ignorance because intelligent isn’t the right term that’s for sure. You set up everything specifically to cater equipment, skill level, muscle group and it comes up with something somewhat catered to your request. Don’t worry that exercise in there with equipment you don’t have should have a substitute around you somewhere. Oh you want to replace it, let me show you seven exercises that aren’t equivalent. Oh you don’t want to have a buttload of routines in your face or your archive, well you better do the same three routines because removing anything deletes your workout history and your results for future routines. We know we said it’s intelligent, but we only say that to swindle people. 

By the way: Customer service should be simply that instead they point the finger at the paying customers like a bad ex saying it’s not me IT’S YOU!

reviews.title: So far not good
reviews.text: I downloaded to use with my Apple Watch. I really thought I would end up getting subscription. Glad there is a trial. App does not ask about conditions like bad knees or back. App does ask about equipment you have, but then gives you exercises that needs equipment you don’t have. After working out, it still shows no workout being completed on watch. I did the cycling twice and still shows nothing. It is very hard to navigate. I couldn’t find the timer for the cycling until the second time. It does show activities completed in a sense that they have a checkmark once you go into it deeper, but main screen still says 0 workouts complete,  0 exercises, 0 minutes. Really wanted this to work. Maybe it’s better after you buy subscription, but I’m not buying something that doesn’t seem to work.
